paragraphs.title: The Anointing and the Signs on the Journey

answers: He anointed him with oil
He gave him a book
He sent him to battle
easy.explanation: Samuel poured oil upon Saul’s head and told him that the Lord had anointed him.
easy.q: What did Samuel do to Saul at the beginning of the passage?

answers: That he had been chosen as king
That the asses had been found
That the prophets were waiting for him
easy.explanation: They were to tell Saul that the asses had been found and that his father was concerned about him.
easy.q: What were the two men supposed to tell Saul?

answers: One loaf
Three loaves
Three loaves carried by each man
easy.explanation: One of the three men carried three loaves of bread.
easy.q: How many loaves of bread did one of the men at the plain of Tabor carry?

answers: Two loaves of bread
A bottle of wine
Three kids
medium.explanation: The men were to salute Saul and give him two loaves of bread.
medium.q: What was Saul supposed to receive from the men at the plain of Tabor?

answers: He was supposed to find the asses
The Spirit of the Lord was to come upon him, and he was to prophesy
He was supposed to wait for seven men
medium.explanation: Saul was to meet a company of prophets, and the Spirit of the Lord was to come upon him.
medium.q: What was supposed to happen to Saul at the hill of God?

answers: A military outpost or stationed force
Loaves of bread
Musical instruments
medium.explanation: A garrison is a group of soldiers stationed in a particular place.
medium.q: In the phrase “the garrison of the Philistines,” what does “garrison” mean?

answers: Only his return to searching for the asses
His transition into a new role and God’s guidance on his journey
The cancellation of his anointing
challenge.explanation: The signs were meant to confirm Saul’s transition into his new role and strengthen him on the way.
challenge.q: What did the series of signs given to Saul represent?

answers: Wait seven days until Samuel came
Continue immediately to his home
Gather all the prophets
challenge.explanation: Samuel told Saul to wait seven days until he came and showed him what to do.
challenge.q: What was Saul required to do after going to Gilgal?

answers: Prophets, men with bread, two men near Rachel’s sepulchre
Two men near Rachel’s sepulchre, men with bread, a company of prophets
Men with bread, a company of prophets, two men near Rachel’s sepulchre
challenge.explanation: First Saul met two men, then three men carrying bread, and finally a company of prophets.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the signs along the way?

paragraphs.title: Saul Prophesies and Becomes a Different Person

answers: God gave him another heart
He lost his way
He returned to search for the asses
easy.explanation: The passage says that God gave Saul another heart.
easy.q: What happened to Saul after he turned his back to go from Samuel?

answers: A company of prophets
The Philistine army
The family of Matri
easy.explanation: A company of prophets met Saul at the hill.
easy.q: Who met Saul at the hill?

answers: With his uncle
With the prophets
With the men of Benjamin
easy.explanation: The Spirit of God came upon Saul, and he prophesied among the prophets.

answers: They saw him prophesying among the prophets
They saw him find the asses
They heard him command the army
medium.explanation: They had known Saul before, so they were astonished when they saw him prophesying.
medium.q: What caused the people who had known Saul to wonder?

answers: Is Saul also among the prophets?
Saul at Gilgal
Saul among the asses
medium.explanation: The people asked, “Is Saul also among the prophets?” and the saying became a proverb.
medium.q: What proverb arose because of Saul’s action?

answers: A group or gathering
A musical instrument
A mountain road
medium.explanation: Here, “company” means a group of prophets.
medium.q: In the phrase “a company of prophets,” what does “company” mean?

answers: The Spirit caused him to prophesy and appear as a different man
The Spirit caused him to hide the asses
The Spirit caused him to leave Samuel immediately
challenge.explanation: The Spirit of God came upon Saul, and he prophesied and behaved differently.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the Spirit of God and Saul’s change?

answers: Saul had always been known as a prophet
It was surprising to see a familiar man prophesying
The prophets refused to speak with him
challenge.explanation: The people were surprised because Saul’s new behavior differed from what they had previously known about him.
challenge.q: Why did the question “Is Saul also among the prophets?” become a proverb?

answers: He came to the high place
He returned to his father’s house
He went to Gilgal
challenge.explanation: After he finished prophesying, Saul came to the high place.
challenge.q: What did Saul do after he finished prophesying?

paragraphs.title: The Return Home and the Hidden Kingship

answers: His uncle
Samuel
The king of the Philistines
easy.explanation: Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant where they had gone.
easy.q: Whom did Saul meet after he returned?

answers: To search for the asses
To search for prophets
To choose a king
easy.explanation: Saul said that they had gone to seek the asses.
easy.q: Why had Saul and his servant originally gone out?

answers: That the asses had been found
That he had been anointed king
That he would wait at Gilgal
easy.explanation: Saul told his uncle plainly that the asses were found.
easy.q: What did Saul tell his uncle?

answers: What Samuel had said to them
Who the three men were
What the children of Belial had done
medium.explanation: His uncle asked Saul to tell him what Samuel had said to them.
medium.q: What did Saul’s uncle ask him to tell him?

answers: That the asses had been found
The matter of the kingdom
That they had gone to seek the asses
medium.explanation: Saul told him about the asses but did not tell him about the matter of the kingdom.
medium.q: What did Saul not tell his uncle?

answers: He was still embarrassed by the appointment and did not understand its meaning
The asses had not been found
Samuel had forbidden him to speak with his uncle
medium.explanation: His silence reflects Saul’s embarrassment and his incomplete understanding of the appointment.
medium.q: Why, according to the idea of the passage, did Saul hide the matter of the kingdom?

answers: He hurried to announce that he had been chosen
He kept the matter of the kingdom to himself
He openly opposed Samuel
challenge.explanation: Saul told only about the asses and kept the matter of the kingdom private.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Saul’s response about his behavior at this stage?

answers: The uncle asks about all Samuel’s words, but Saul answers only part of the matter
The uncle asks about the asses, but Saul answers about the kingdom
The uncle does not want to know anything, but Saul tells everything
challenge.explanation: The uncle asks what Samuel said, but Saul reports only that the asses had been found.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the uncle’s question and Saul’s answer?

answers: He mentioned that the asses were found but omitted the matter of the kingdom
He said that the prophets were not found
He said that he waited seven days at Gilgal
challenge.explanation: The important detail is that Saul mentioned the asses but omitted the matter of the kingdom.
challenge.q: Which detail in Saul’s answer is easy to miss?

paragraphs.title: The Selection of the King Before the People

answers: At Mizpeh
At Bethel
At the hill of God
easy.explanation: Samuel called the people together unto the Lord at Mizpeh.
easy.q: Where did Samuel gather the people?

answers: The tribe of Judah
The tribe of Benjamin
The tribe of Ephraim
easy.explanation: The tribe of Benjamin was taken.
easy.q: Which tribe was taken in the selection?

answers: At the high place
Among the stuff
At Samuel’s house
easy.explanation: The Lord revealed that Saul had hidden himself among the stuff.
easy.q: Where was Saul when they sought to bring him forward?

answers: God’s deliverance and their demand for a king
Saul’s journey with his servant
The musical instruments of the prophets
medium.explanation: Samuel reminded them that the Lord had delivered them, yet they had asked for a king.
medium.q: What did Samuel remind the people of before the selection?

Saul the son of Kish, Benjamin, the family of Matri
The family of Matri, Saul the son of Kish, Benjamin
medium.explanation: First Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and finally Saul.
medium.q: What was the order of the selection that led to Saul?

answers: Refused or cast aside
Praised greatly
Searched for on the road
medium.explanation: Samuel said that the people had refused God’s rule when they demanded a king.
medium.q: In the sentence “ye have this day rejected your God,” what does “rejected” mean?

answers: The people asked for a king even though the Lord had saved them
The Lord had never saved Israel
The people had not asked for a king
challenge.explanation: Samuel recalled the Lord’s deliverance and contrasted it with the people’s demand for a king.
challenge.q: What did Samuel emphasize in his speech about the people’s demand for a king?

answers: He was taller than all the people
He was older than all the people
He was the only one carrying a musical instrument
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Saul was higher than any of the people from his shoulders upward.
challenge.q: What was Saul’s most noticeable characteristic when he was presented to the people?

answers: Instructions concerning the order of kingship, written in a book before the Lord
A list of the prophets’ names
Instructions for searching for the asses
challenge.explanation: Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the Lord.
challenge.q: What did “the manner of the kingdom” include?

paragraphs.title: Acceptance of Saul and Opposition to Him

answers: To Gibeah
To Mizpeh
To Gilgal
A band of men whose hearts God had touched
All the children of Belial
The whole company of prophets
easy.explanation: A band of men whose hearts God had touched went with Saul.

answers: He held his peace
He punished them
He left Gibeah
easy.explanation: Saul held his peace and did not answer them.
easy.q: How did Saul respond to the children of Belial?

answers: They praised him and brought him presents
They despised him and brought him no presents
They accompanied him home
medium.explanation: They questioned how Saul could save them, despised him, and brought no presents.
medium.q: What did the children of Belial do toward Saul?

answers: Some supported him while others despised him
Everyone opposed him
Everyone immediately left him
medium.explanation: Some men whose hearts God had touched went with Saul, while the children of Belial rejected him.
medium.q: What does the contrast between the two groups around Saul show?

answers: He remained silent and did not respond
He shouted to the people
He played a musical instrument
medium.explanation: To hold one’s peace means to remain silent and not answer.
medium.q: What does the phrase “he held his peace” mean?

answers: He chose not to respond to their contempt
He gave up the kingdom
He asked Samuel to punish them
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that Saul held his peace instead of answering their opposition.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Saul’s response to the children of Belial?

answers: Men who were moved to support Saul
Men who had been wounded in battle
Men who belonged to the company of prophets
challenge.explanation: These men were moved by God to go with and support Saul.
challenge.q: What does “whose hearts God had touched” mean in this context?

answers: Saul is supported by some, while others despise him
All the people refuse to accept Saul
Saul disappears and cannot be found
challenge.explanation: The ending presents both support for Saul and opposition to him.
challenge.q: What tension appears at the end of the chapter?
